chunks: My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn Miskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (AS), who said: I heard him say

And with him were a group of people debating about deeds and actions, so he said: The ability precedes the action. Allah, the Mighty and High, did not command anything of grasping or expanding except that the servant is capable of it.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between divine command and human capability in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the theological principle that divine command (*taklif*) necessitates human capability (*istita'ah*), asserting that the power to act precedes the act itself. This establishes the Shia doctrine that God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity, as the servant is inherently equipped to fulfill the specific actions commanded, such as grasping or expanding. This reasoning reinforces the concept of *Adl* (Divine Justice) by linking the obligation directly to the pre-existing ability of the servant.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 21. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn alHusayn, on the authority of both Abu Shu`ayb al-Mahamili and Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Muskan, on the authority of Abu Basir that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said: When a group of people were debating before him about the deeds and actins, I heard him say, “
The ability to act precedes the action. Allah, the Mighty and High, did not command anything that would cause fear or delight until He granted His Servant with the ability to act.”
